items.stem: Explain the difference between an automated machine and an autonomous robot.
items.answer: An automated machine repeats pre-programmed actions in a controlled setting (e.g. a fixed welding arm); an autonomous robot senses and adapts to changing environments, making some decisions without human input (e.g. a delivery robot).
items.markingKey: An automated machine repeats pre-programmed actions in a controlled setting (e.g. a fixed welding arm); an autonomous robot senses and adapts to changing environments, making some decisions without human input (e.g. a delivery robot). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why sensors are essential for a robot to operate autonomously.
items.answer: Without sensors a robot cannot detect obstacles, objects or changes in its environment, so it could only repeat fixed movements; sensor data lets the controller adjust actions in real time.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Without sensors a robot cannot detect obstacles, objects or changes in its environment, so it could only repeat fixed movements; sensor data lets the controller adjust actions in real time. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.answer: Drivers who believe Level 2 cars drive themselves may stop paying attention (automation complacency), causing crashes; marketing names like "Autopilot" may encourage this.

items.answer: HEATER OFF, HEATER OFF, HEATER ON, HEATER OFF, HEATER OFF; each action counteracts the deviation from the target, keeping temperature stable

items.stem: Briefly explain why the "sense–think–act" cycle describes how robots work.
items.answer: Robots repeatedly gather data from sensors (sense), process it with algorithms to decide what to do (think) and move using actuators (act); the results change what is sensed next, forming a feedback loop.

items.stem: "Self-driving cars on sale today are fully autonomous." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Most consumer systems (e.g. Tesla Autopilot) are SAE Level 2 driver assistance requiring constant supervision; robotaxis like Waymo operate at Level 4 only in defined areas.

items.stem: Briefly describe the Roomba (2002) and explain what it reveals about robots in everyday life.
items.answer: iRobot's Roomba vacuum used bump and cliff sensors and simple behaviours; later models map homes with cameras. A simple sense–act design brought robots into millions of homes, while home-mapping later raised privacy concerns.

items.stem: Using Zipline in Rwanda as an example, explain robots in health logistics.
items.answer: Since 2016 Zipline's fixed-wing drones have delivered blood and medical supplies to hospitals across Rwanda, parachuting packages to the destination. Autonomous delivery overcame poor road access, reducing delivery times and waste of blood products.

A robot that performs useful tasks for people outside industrial automation, such as cleaning, delivery or hospitality
The hypothesis (Masahiro Mori, 1970) that robots that look almost, but not quite, human cause feelings of unease
A programmable robot arm or machine used in manufacturing for tasks such as welding, painting, assembly and packaging

items.stem: A student claims: "Self-driving cars on sale today are fully autonomous." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Most consumer systems (e.g. Tesla Autopilot) are SAE Level 2 driver assistance requiring constant supervision; robotaxis like Waymo operate at Level 4 only in defined areas.
items.markingKey: Most consumer systems (e.g. Tesla Autopilot) are SAE Level 2 driver assistance requiring constant supervision; robotaxis like Waymo operate at Level 4 only in defined areas. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between a surgical robot and an autonomous robot.
items.answer: A surgical robot such as da Vinci is controlled by a surgeon and enhances precision (tele-operated); an autonomous robot makes decisions and acts without continuous human control.
items.markingKey: A surgical robot such as da Vinci is controlled by a surgeon and enhances precision (tele-operated); an autonomous robot makes decisions and acts without continuous human control. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between anthropomorphism and the uncanny valley.
items.answer: Anthropomorphism is our tendency to see human traits in robots; the uncanny valley is the discomfort felt when a robot looks almost human but not quite.
items.markingKey: Anthropomorphism is our tendency to see human traits in robots; the uncanny valley is the discomfort felt when a robot looks almost human but not quite. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between a sensor and an actuator.
items.answer: A sensor takes in information from the environment (input); an actuator produces movement or action in the environment (output).
items.markingKey: A sensor takes in information from the environment (input); an actuator produces movement or action in the environment (output). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "Surgical robots perform operations by themselves." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Systems like da Vinci are controlled by a surgeon at a console; the robot translates hand movements into precise instrument movements.
items.markingKey: Systems like da Vinci are controlled by a surgeon at a console; the robot translates hand movements into precise instrument movements. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "If a robot shows emotions, it must feel them." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Robots can simulate emotional expressions through programmed responses; there is no evidence that current robots have feelings or consciousness.
items.markingKey: Robots can simulate emotional expressions through programmed responses; there is no evidence that current robots have feelings or consciousness. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
A robot vacuum cleaner uses an ultrasonic distance sensor and this control algorithm:

loop for each sensor reading DIST (cm)
    if DIST < 20 then
        output "TURN"
    else
        output "FORWARD"
    end if
end loop

The sensor readings are 47, 56, 33, 15. State the outputs in order.
items.answer: FORWARD, FORWARD, FORWARD, TURN
items.markingKey: 47 ≥ 20 → FORWARD; 56 ≥ 20 → FORWARD; 33 ≥ 20 → FORWARD; 15 < 20 → TURN [A1 per two correct, max 2].

items.stem: A delivery drone flies at 110 km/h carrying medicines to an island clinic, 45 km away. Calculate the one-way flight time in minutes. By road the route is 40% longer and vehicles average 30 km/h. Calculate the time saved by the drone.
items.answer: 24.5 minutes; road 126.0 min; saves 101.5 min

items.stem: Using the "emergency evacuation" trust experiment as an example, explain over-trust in robots.
items.answer: In a 2016 Georgia Tech study, participants followed a robot during a simulated fire alarm even after it had previously malfunctioned and pointed towards a dark room. People over-trusted a robot in an emergency, showing the need for trust calibration in design.
items.markingKey: Context (In a 2016 Georgia Tech study, participants followed a robot during a simulated fire alarm even after it had previously malfunctioned and pointed towards a dark room.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: people over-trusted a robot in an emergency, showing the need for trust calibration in design. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to over-trust in robots.

items.stem: A smart thermostat (target 20 °C) switches the heater ON if the temperature is below 19.5 °C, OFF if above 20.5 °C, and makes no change otherwise. Readings: 22.9 °C, 18.4 °C, 22.0 °C, 19.7 °C, 21.5 °C. State the action for each reading. Explain why this is negative feedback.
items.answer: HEATER OFF, HEATER ON, HEATER OFF, NO CHANGE, HEATER OFF; each action counteracts the deviation from the target, keeping temperature stable
items.markingKey: 22.9 → HEATER OFF; 18.4 → HEATER ON; 22.0 → HEATER OFF; 19.7 → NO CHANGE; 21.5 → HEATER OFF [A1 A1]. Output opposes the change, stabilising the system [R1].

items.stem: Outline one way in which Zipline in Rwanda shows robots in health logistics.
items.answer: Since 2016 Zipline's fixed-wing drones have delivered blood and medical supplies to hospitals across Rwanda, parachuting packages to the destination. Autonomous delivery overcame poor road access, reducing delivery times and waste of blood products.
items.markingKey: Context (Since 2016 Zipline's fixed-wing drones have delivered blood and medical supplies to hospitals across Rwanda, parachuting packages to the destination.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: autonomous delivery overcame poor road access, reducing delivery times and waste of blood products. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to robots in health logistics.

items.stem: Using Sophia's "citizenship" (2017) as an example, explain anthropomorphism and its politics.
items.answer: Saudi Arabia announced citizenship for Hanson Robotics' humanoid robot Sophia at a technology conference, drawing criticism given limited rights for many humans in the country. Treating a robot as a person was a publicity act that highlighted confusion about robot capabilities and rights.
items.markingKey: Context (Saudi Arabia announced citizenship for Hanson Robotics' humanoid robot Sophia at a technology conference, drawing criticism given limited rights for many humans in the country.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: treating a robot as a person was a publicity act that highlighted confusion about robot capabilities and rights. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to anthropomorphism and its politics.

items.stem: Briefly describe Waymo robotaxis and explain what it reveals about sensors and high autonomy.
items.answer: Waymo launched a public driverless ride-hailing service in Phoenix in 2020 and later expanded to San Francisco and Los Angeles, using LiDAR, radar and cameras. Multiple sensors and machine learning allow Level 4 driving in mapped areas without a human driver.
items.markingKey: Context (Waymo launched a public driverless ride-hailing service in Phoenix in 2020 and later expanded to San Francisco and Los Angeles, using LiDAR, radar and cameras.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Outline two points that could be used to evaluate the claim: "Robots have improved working conditions more than they have worsened them."
items.answer: Robots have made some jobs safer but can intensify others; outcomes depend on how they are introduced and on worker voice.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: take over dangerous, dirty and dull tasks (welding, nuclear inspection); cobots reduce strain. Arguments against: work intensification and surveillance in warehouses; job losses in routine manufacturing; deskilling. Supported judgement: Robots have made some jobs safer but can intensify others; outcomes depend on how they are introduced and on worker voice.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "Social robots can meet people's emotional needs."
items.answer: Social robots can support emotional well-being but cannot replace genuine human relationships; they should complement human care.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: comfort and companionship (Paro); consistency and patience in care settings. Arguments against: simulated, not real, empathy; may reduce human contact; privacy concerns from constant monitoring. Supported judgement: Social robots can support emotional well-being but cannot replace genuine human relationships; they should complement human care. Upper-middle – relevant examples and some balance; conclusion reasoned. Middle – some relevant knowledge, partly descriptive; conclusion stated. Lower – limited, general knowledge, mainly descriptive. Bottom – minimal relevant material.

items.stem: "Robots should be defined by their autonomy rather than their appearance." How far do you agree? Refer to at least one Digital Society concept in your answer.
items.answer: Autonomy is the more useful defining feature for analysis, but appearance matters for social impacts.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: autonomy determines capabilities, risks and responsibility; most robots are not humanoid. Arguments against: appearance shapes how people interact with robots (anthropomorphism); tele-operated machines are also robots. Supported judgement: Autonomy is the more useful defining feature for analysis, but appearance matters for social impacts.
